title: Cache Telemetry Cardinality Budget (Series Count Estimates + Sampling Plan)
content:
Purpose
- Estimate time series counts for new prefix/KV cache metrics under different label sets.
- Propose a safe default label allowlist (runtime + gateway + ingestion).
- Define sampling/rate-limit strategies so we can ship dashboards + alerts without exploding series or spend.

Context
- Metrics introduced in runtime PRs: 18421/18422/18423/18424/18430 (+ renames 18431).
- Joinability needs route/model/version/deployment_mode tags (ENG-4823), but we must avoid per-tenant explosions.
- SRE requirement: be able to slice by model, route (top-N), deployment mode, region, and request-shape buckets.

Terminology / Counting model
- “Series” ~= unique combination of metric name + labelset + (for histograms) bucket label.
- For Prom-style histograms: series_per_histogram = base_series * (num_buckets + 2) [includes +Inf and _sum/_count depending on backend].
- For simplicity below, we assume histograms emit: buckets + _sum + _count => (B + 2). Confirm against metrics backend.

Assumptions (edit if these drift)
- env: 3 values (staging, canary, prod)
- region: 6 values (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-1)
- deployment_mode: 3 values (hosted, dedicated, private)
- model_family: 6 values (llama, mistral, qwen, gemma, mixtral, other)
- model_id (Redwood internal model name): 40 values (current catalog + active pinned variants)
- model_version: 200 values (rolling; high risk label)
- route_id: 2,000 values in prod (high risk label)
- tenant_id: 8,000 values in prod (do NOT allow)
- cache_policy: 2 values (enabled, disabled)
- cache_layer: 2 values (prefix, kv)
- miss_reason: 6 values (capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch, other)
- prompt_len_bucket: 10 values (0-128, 129-256, 257-512, 513-1k, 1-2k, 2-4k, 4-8k, 8-16k, 16-32k, 32k+)
- reuse_depth_bucket (prefix reuse depth): 8 values
- token_hist_bucket (token count histogram bins): 10 values
- time window: counts are for “steady state” (not cumulative over days); but label churn (model_version) creates churn and storage/compute overhead.

Label policy proposal (TL;DR)
- Allowed always: env, region, deployment_mode, model_family, model_id, cache_layer
- Allowed sometimes (guarded): route_id (only for top-N routes per region/model, plus allowlist), miss_reason (only for miss counters), prompt_len_bucket (only on histograms)
- Explicitly disallowed: tenant_id, raw path, request_id, prompt_hash, user_id
- Strong recommendation: do NOT label by model_version in metrics (use traces/logs/analytics table for version-level; or keep version only in sampled traces). If absolutely needed, constrain to “current + previous” (2 values) per model_id and region.

==============================
Sheet 1 — Candidate label sets
==============================
Legend
- Base labels = env, region, deployment_mode
- “Model slice” = + model_family, model_id
- “Route slice” = + route_id (guarded)
- “Shape slice” = + prompt_len_bucket and/or token_hist_bucket

Labelset A (Minimal / safe default)
- env, region, deployment_mode, cache_layer

Labelset B (Recommended for dashboards)
- env, region, deployment_mode, cache_layer, model_family, model_id

Labelset C (Dashboards + shape)
- env, region, deployment_mode, cache_layer, model_family, model_id, prompt_len_bucket

Labelset D (Route triage, guarded)
- env, region, deployment_mode, cache_layer, model_family, model_id, route_id

Labelset E (Route + shape, guarded)
- env, region, deployment_mode, cache_layer, model_family, model_id, route_id, prompt_len_bucket

Labelset F (NOT recommended — version)
- env, region, deployment_mode, cache_layer, model_family, model_id, model_version

=======================================
Sheet 2 — Series estimates (by labelset)
=======================================
Base cardinalities
- env=3
- region=6
- deployment_mode=3
- cache_layer=2
- model_family=6
- model_id=40
- prompt_len_bucket=10
- route_id=2,000 (but guarded)
- model_version=200 (high churn)

Computed base series per metric (counter/gauge) = product of label cardinalities

A) Minimal
- 3*6*3*2 = 108 series/metric

B) + model
- 108*6*40 = 25,920 series/metric

C) + model + prompt_len_bucket
- 25,920*10 = 259,200 series/metric

D) + model + route_id (unguarded worst case)
- 25,920*2,000 = 51,840,000 series/metric (NOT OK)

D2) + model + route_id (guarded top-N)
- Assume top-N routes per (region, model_id) = 20
- Effective route_id values per (region, model_id) capped at 20, else aggregated into route_id="__other__"
- Effective route_id cardinality: 21
- Series/metric = 25,920*21 = 544,320 series/metric (high but survivable for a small number of metrics)

E2) + model + route_id (guarded 21) + prompt_len_bucket
- 544,320*10 = 5,443,200 series/metric (only acceptable for 1–2 key metrics, and possibly only in prod)

F) + model_version
- 25,920*200 = 5,184,000 series/metric (and churn)
- Conclusion: do not do this in metrics. Use analytics/traces.

Histogram multiplier
- If histogram buckets B=10 => multiplier (B+2)=12
- Example: labelset C histogram => 259,200 * 12 = 3,110,400 series per histogram metric

============================================
Sheet 3 — Metric-by-metric budget (proposed)
============================================
This is the proposed “what we actually ship” series footprint. Assumes prod only. Staging/canary can be looser since volume is lower, but series is still series.

Metric list (representative; naming per standards doc)
1) redwood_cache_requests_total (counter)
2) redwood_cache_hits_total (counter)
3) redwood_cache_misses_total (counter)
4) redwood_cache_misses_total{miss_reason=} (counter)
5) redwood_cache_evictions_total (counter)
6) redwood_cache_pressure (gauge)
7) redwood_cache_wasted_prefill_tokens_total (counter)
8) redwood_cache_prefix_reuse_tokens (histogram)
9) redwood_cache_kv_reuse_ratio (histogram) [if we keep as histogram]

Proposed labelset per metric
- 1/2/3: Labelset B (model slice) => 25,920 each
- 4: Labelset B + miss_reason (6) => 25,920*6 = 155,520
- 5: Labelset B (optional: eviction_reason label? keep OFF initially) => 25,920
- 6: Labelset B => 25,920
- 7: Labelset B + prompt_len_bucket (C) => 259,200 (wasted prefill is most interpretable by prompt size)
- 8: Histogram with labelset C => 259,200*12 = 3,110,400
- 9: Histogram with labelset B (no shape) => 25,920*12 = 311,040

Subtotal estimate (prod only)
- Counters/gauges: 25,920*5 + 155,520 + 259,200 = 129,600 + 155,520 + 259,200 = 544,320 series
- Histograms: 3,110,400 + 311,040 = 3,421,440 series
- Total ~ 3,965,760 series

Notes
- ~4.0M series is a meaningful footprint but feasible if we avoid route_id and model_version in core metrics.
- If we add route_id (guarded) to even 2–3 core counters, we can add ~0.5M per metric (D2), so keep route slicing limited.

========================================
Sheet 4 — Route slicing plan (guardrails)
========================================
Goal
- Enable route triage for SRE (identify regressions tied to specific routes) without blowing up series.

Proposal
- Add route_id only to the following metrics initially:
  - redwood_cache_hits_total (counter)
  - redwood_cache_misses_total (counter)
- Use guarded route_id labeling:
  - Ingestion keeps per-route series only for top-N routes by request volume per (env, region, deployment_mode, model_id) per 24h.
  - All other routes aggregated into route_id="__other__".
  - N = 20 default; configurable per env.

Series impact (prod)
- Two metrics at labelset D2 => 544,320 * 2 = 1,088,640 additional series
- Total becomes ~5.05M series (still OK, but watch). If we also add prompt_len_bucket with route labels, it explodes to ~5.4M per metric; avoid.

Operational note
- This needs an ingestion-side “top-N keeper” (observability-pack PR-613 direction) OR gateway-side label suppression based on local LRU/topK (riskier for correctness).

=================================
Sheet 5 — Sampling / rate limiting
=================================
Cardinality controls ≠ volume controls. We need both.

A) Sampling for high-frequency event-like metrics
- For per-request metrics emitted in runtime hot path, sample at request-level:
  - default sample_rate = 0.10 (10%) in prod for “debug-only” dimensions (e.g., detailed miss reason + prompt_len_bucket together)
  - sample_rate = 1.00 (100%) for core hit/miss counters without route_id/model_version

B) Local rate limiting (runtime)
- Add token-bucket limiter to avoid spikes when a bad config causes huge event emission:
  - max_events_per_sec_per_instance = 5,000 (tune)
  - overflow behavior: increment a single counter redwood_cache_telemetry_dropped_total{reason="rate_limit"}

C) Ingestion-side drop/aggregate rules
- Hard drop forbidden labels (tenant_id, raw_path, prompt_hash)
- Enforce allowlist per metric name:
  - e.g., miss_reason allowed only on *_misses_total
  - route_id allowed only on *_hits_total and *_misses_total
  - prompt_len_bucket allowed only on histograms + wasted_prefill
- If disallowed label combination detected, rewrite to label="__dropped__" (preferred) or drop series entirely (last resort).

D) Model version handling
- Metrics: keep model_version OFF.
- Traces: allow model_version tag on spans with sampling (e.g., 1–5%) for deep dives.
- Analytics: create daily aggregate table keyed by (date, region, deployment_mode, model_id, model_version, route_id_bucket, prompt_len_bucket) for backtests + recommendations.

======================================
Sheet 6 — Proposed budgets + thresholds
======================================
Budget targets (prod)
- Total new cache telemetry series budget: 6,000,000 max (target 4,000,000)
- Per-metric max series:
  - Any counter/gauge: <= 600,000
  - Any histogram: <= 3,500,000

Alerting thresholds (for telemetry health, not cache efficiency)
- Telemetry drop counter (ingestion rewrite/drop):
  - redwood_cache_telemetry_dropped_total rate > 0.5% of cache metrics ingress for 10m => page Telemetry oncall
- Missing label rate:
  - % of series with route_id="__missing__" > 1% for 30m => ticket ENG-Platform

================================
Sheet 7 — Open questions / TODO
================================
1) Confirm histogram emission format
- Are we emitting classic Prom buckets + _sum/_count, or OTEL exponential hist? Update multiplier accordingly.

2) Confirm model_id cardinality assumption
- Current catalog is ~40, but Dedicated/Private can pin custom builds. Need enforcement: model_id must be from control-plane registry, not arbitrary strings.

3) How to define “top-N routes”
- By request count or token count? SRE preference: token count (cost driver). Telemetry preference: request count (stable, cheaper).
- Proposed: top-N by request count, with “heavy hitter” override by token volume weekly.

4) Prompt length bucketing
- Are the buckets stable across hosted/dedicated/private? If not, standardize in runtime instrumentation.

5) Version-level troubleshooting
- Support wants to debug SUP-3912-like issues (version mismatch). Proposal: rely on miss_reason=version_mismatch in metrics + sampled traces with model_version.

Change log
- 2025-03-06: Initial estimates + labelset options (Caleb)
- 2025-03-08: Added guarded top-N route plan + budgets (Caleb, Allison)
- 2025-03-10: Aligned with runtime sampling flags + rate limiting (Thomas, Omar)
- 2025-03-12: Updated miss_reason cardinality to 6 and added telemetry-health thresholds (Nadia)
